We need to list elements that can be definitively identified based on isotope distribution patterns visible in the mass spectrum. We need the mass spectrum data. Use mass_spectrometry_spectra tool. Then analyze isotopic patterns: look for characteristic isotopic spacing and relative intensities. For example: Chlorine (Cl) shows M and M+2 peaks with ~3:1 ratio. Bromine (Br) shows M and M+2 with ~1:1. Sulfur (S) shows M+2 ~4% of M. Carbon shows M+1 ~1.1% per carbon. Hydrogen shows M+1 ~0.015% per H (negligible). Nitrogen shows M+1 ~0.37% per N. Oxygen shows M+2 due to 18O ~0.2% per O. But we need definitive identification: likely elements with distinctive isotopic patterns: Cl, Br, S, maybe Si (but not in list). Also maybe isotopic patterns for C (C13) but less distinctive.

We need to get the spectrum. Use tool.
